extracted.intended_audience: members and staff of the Administrative Conference, researchers, committee participants, and others interested in how ACUS recommendations and statements are produced
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Administrative Conference's Project Process for producing formal recommendations and occasional 'Statements', enumerating required steps from idea selection through Council and membership consideration to adoption and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: gathering and selecting ideas for a project
rubrics_metrics.description: The process includes: gathering and selecting ideas for a project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the initial phase of the Project Process — identifying topics worthy of study and deciding which ideas will become formal projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: getting Council approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The process includes: getting Council approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before proceeding, proposed projects must be approved by the Conference's Council, indicating an institutional gatekeeping/authorization step.

rubrics_metrics.name: selecting the researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: The process includes: selecting the researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A researcher is chosen to perform the study that will form the basis for a recommendation; selection is a required step in the Project Process.

rubrics_metrics.name: having the researcher’s report considered by a committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The process includes: having the researcher’s report considered by a committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The researcher's report is evaluated by an assigned committee, which reviews findings and implications as part of deliberation toward a recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: having the selected committee formulate a recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The process includes: having the selected committee formulate a recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee synthesizes the research and decides on the language and content of a proposed recommendation to advance to Council/membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: having a committee’s recommendation considered by the Council and then the full Conference membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The process includes: having a committee’s recommendation considered by the Council and then the full Conference membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After committee formulation, recommendations undergo sequential review first by the Council and then by the full Conference membership prior to adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: adoption by voting members at semi-annual plenary sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations are adopted by the voting members of the Conference at semi-annual plenary sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal adoption requires a vote of Conference members at one of the semi-annual plenary meetings — this is the decisive procedural step for making recommendations official.

rubrics_metrics.name: implementation activities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following adoption, the Conference undertakes activities to implement the recommendation or otherwise promote its effects; implementation is treated as part of the Project Process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference Statements (alternative to formal recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the Conference membership has acted to adopt a 'Statement' to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements are typically produced by the same Project Process but may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments rather than formal recommendations; historically ACUS adopted 17 such statements (1968–1995) which are included in the searchable database.
